prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single magic “AI-recommendation” checker. To know whether LLMs like ChatGPT recommend your business you should (A) directly test several AI engines that use current web data and show sources, and (B) manage/update the authoritative data sources those engines draw from. Best-in-class tools for those two jobs are:

- To test and see sources: Perplexity.ai and Bing Chat (both surface citations), Google Bard, ChatGPT with browsing enabled (or GPT-4o with web access), and Anthropic Claude — run the same prompts across them to see whether they mention/recommend your business and what sources they cite.
- To control the data AI uses and influence recommendations: Yext (best for distributing a single “knowledge” profile to many platforms/AI), plus Google Business Profile and Bing Places (free and essential).
- To monitor local presence and rankings across directories: BrightLocal or Moz Local (good for routine checks and citation tracking).

How to do it (practical steps)
1. Claim and optimize authoritative listings (free/first step)
   - Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, and make sure your website has Schema.org localBusiness markup and clear NAP (name, address, phone).
   - Create/claim Wikidata/Wikipedia entries if eligible (many AI/knowledge graphs pull from these).
2. Test LLMs directly
   - Use Perplexity.ai (or Bing Chat) to ask for recommendations — they cite sources so you can see why the model recommended (or didn’t).
   - Ask the same question in ChatGPT (with browsing or plugins enabled), Bard, and Claude to compare answers.
   - Example prompt: “I’m looking for a [category] in [city]. Would you recommend [Business Name, address]? Why or why not? Please list sources.”
3. Monitor & manage
   - If you want automated distribution / control of the facts AI uses, use Yext (paid) to publish your knowledge graph to many platforms, and BrightLocal or Moz to monitor listings and reviews.
   - Track reviews and citation consistency — many LLMs rely on review aggregate and knowledge panels.
4. Improve your odds of being recommended
   - Keep NAP consistent, get good reviews, add structured data, publish a clear “About” and FAQ on your site, get local backlinks, and aim for a Knowledge Panel (Google).

Which to pick?
- If your goal is “see whether ChatGPT/Bard/others will recommend me” — start with Perplexity (sources) and run tests on ChatGPT/Bard/Bing.
- If your goal is “make AI more likely to recommend my business” — invest in Yext + optimize Google Business Profile + run BrightLocal monitoring.
- If budget is limited — do the listings + schema + manual LLM testing (free) regularly.

If you want, tell me your business name, category, and city and I can run a set of sample prompts you can paste into different LLMs and suggest the most effective next steps.
